Chord diagram of taxon-group relationships

Source: R/mp_chord.R
mp_chord.Rd

Draws a circular chord diagram with circlize connecting the top taxa at a chosen rank to the levels of a grouping variable, with ribbon widths proportional to mean (relative) abundance. Like mp_circos() this draws to the current graphics device (the exception to the ggplot contract) and returns the underlying taxon-by-group matrix invisibly.

Usage

mp_chord(
  object,
  group.by,
  tax.level = "Phylum",
  top.n = 12,
  relative = TRUE,
  palette = NULL,
  gap = 2,
  start.degree = 90,
  transparency = 0.5,
  directional = 0,
  title = NULL,
  verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE)
)

Arguments

object

A phyloseq::phyloseq object.

group.by

Sample-metadata column defining the groups (columns of the diagram).

tax.level

Taxonomic rank to agglomerate to (rows of the diagram).

top.n

Number of most-abundant taxa to show; the rest collapse into an "Other" sector.

relative

Use relative abundance (TRUE) or raw counts.

palette

Palette name or colour vector for the taxa sectors/ribbons.

gap

Gap (degrees) between sectors.

start.degree

Starting angle.

transparency

Ribbon transparency in [0, 1].

directional

Passed to circlize::chordDiagram(): 0 (undirected), 1 (taxa to groups) or -1.

title

Optional plot title.

verbose

Print the methods used.

Value

Invisibly, the taxon-by-group abundance matrix that was drawn.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")
mp_chord(GlobalPatterns, group.by = "SampleType", tax.level = "Phylum")
} # }
